title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your daily routine and habits, and say what you and others are doing right now.
intro: This unit is about verbs. Odia has two present tenses: the **simple present** for habits (ମୁଁ ସକାଳେ ଚା ପିଏ 'I drink tea in the morning') and the **present continuous** in **-ଉଛି** for what is happening now (ମୁଁ ଚା ପିଉଛି 'I'm drinking tea'). Endings change for person and respect — never for gender.

vocab.note: Present: ମୁଁ ଶୁଏ, ତୁମେ ଶୁଅ, ଆପଣ ଶୁଅନ୍ତି.
Present ଯାଏ, past ଗଲି, future ଯିବି — irregular.
Present: ମୁଁ ଦିଏ, ଆପଣ ଦିଅନ୍ତି; past: ଦେଲି.
Present: ମୁଁ ନିଏ, ଆପଣ ନିଅନ୍ତି; past: ନେଲି.

phrases.en: What time do you usually get up?
I get up at half past six.
I go to the office every day.
In the evening I go for a walk.
I go to bed late at night.
He/She is having a bath right now. (respectful)

grammar.title: Simple present (habitual)
grammar.body:
Use the simple present for habits and general facts. Take the stem (dictionary form minus **-ିବା**: କରିବା → କର୍-) and add:

ମୁଁ କରେ *kôre* — I do
ଆମେ କରୁ *kôru* — we do
ତୁ କରୁ *kôru* — you do (intimate)
ତୁମେ କର *kôrô* — you do (familiar)
ଆପଣ କରନ୍ତି *kôrônti* — you do (formal)
ସେ କରେ *kôre* — he/she does
ସେ / ସେମାନେ କରନ୍ତି *kôrônti* — he/she (respectful) / they do

Vowel-stem verbs contract: ଖାଇବା → ମୁଁ **ଖାଏ**, ତୁମେ **ଖାଅ**, ଆପଣ **ଖାଆନ୍ତି**; ଯିବା → **ଯାଏ, ଯାଅ, ଯାଆନ୍ତି**; ଶୋଇବା → **ଶୁଏ, ଶୁଅ, ଶୁଅନ୍ତି**. Note: the respectful form is the same as the plural.

Negative: add **ନାହିଁ** after the verb (ମୁଁ ଖାଏ ନାହିଁ); in speech this shrinks to **-ନି** (ଖାଏନି, କରେନି).

examples.en: We eat at nine at night.
When do you go to sleep?

grammar.title: Present continuous: -ଉଛି
grammar.body:
For actions happening **now**, add **-ଉଛି** to the stem, then the person ending:

ମୁଁ କରୁଛି *kôruchhi* · ଆମେ କରୁଛୁ *kôruchhu* · ତୁ କରୁଛୁ · ତୁମେ କରୁଛ *kôruchhô* · ଆପଣ କରୁଛନ୍ତି *kôruchhônti* · ସେ କରୁଛି · ସେମାନେ କରୁଛନ୍ତି.

Vowel stems: ଖାଉଛି, ଯାଉଛି, ପିଉଛି, ଦେଉଛି, ନେଉଛି, ଶୋଉଛି, ଗାଧୋଉଛି.

Negative: **-ଉ ନାହିଁ** (colloquial **-ଉନି**): ମୁଁ ଦେଖୁ ନାହିଁ 'I'm not watching'. Just as in English, the continuous can also refer to the near future: ମୁଁ ଆସୁଛି 'I'm coming'.

examples.en: I'm not watching TV, I'm studying.

dialogue.title: Early birds
dialogue.setting: Sam and Lipi compare their daily routines.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Lipi, what time do you get up every day?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: I get up at half past five.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ବୋଉ ସହିତ ପୂଜା କରେ, ତା'ପରେ ପଢ଼େ। ସାଢ଼େ ନଅଟାରେ କଲେଜ ଯାଏ।
lines.roman: bou sôhitô puja kôre, tapôre pôṛhe. saṛhe nôṭare kôlejô jae.
lines.en: I do puja with Mum, then I study. At half past nine I go to college.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: What do you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ଘରକୁ ଫେରି ଚା ପିଏ, ଆଉ ଭାଇକୁ ପଢ଼ାଏ। ଆଉ ତୁମେ?
lines.roman: ghôrôku pheri cha pie, au bhaiku pôṛhae. au tume?
lines.en: I come home, have tea, and teach my brother. And you?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଆଠଟାରେ ଉଠେ। ନଅଟାରେ ଅଫିସ୍ ଯାଏ, ଛଅଟାରେ ଫେରେ।
lines.roman: muṃ sadharôṇôtô aṭhôṭare uṭhe. nôṭare ôphis jae, chhôṭare phere.
lines.en: I usually get up at eight. I go to the office at nine and come back at six.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: What do you do at night?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ରାନ୍ଧେ, ଟିକେ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ପଢ଼େ, ଆଉ ଏଗାରଟାରେ ଶୁଏ।
lines.roman: muṃ randhe, ṭike Oṛia pôṛhe, au egarôṭare sue.
lines.en: I cook, study a bit of Odia, and go to bed at eleven.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: Wow, you're a very good student!

culture: Many Odia households start the day early with a bath and a short **ପୂଜା** (prayer) before breakfast; cooking often begins only after bathing. Afternoons in the hot season are for a nap — shops in small towns may close between about 1 and 4 p.m. — and evenings are the social time, when people stroll, visit the market or gather at tea stalls.

lessons.title: Getting up and going to bed

tip.title: Habits: the simple present
tip.body:
- Habits use the simple present: ମୁଁ **ଉଠେ**, ଆମେ **ଉଠୁ**, ତୁମେ **ଉଠ**, ସେ **ଉଠେ**, ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ **ଉଠନ୍ତି**.
- Vowel stems shrink: ଶୋଇବା → ମୁଁ **ଶୁଏ**; ଗାଧୋଇବା → ମୁଁ **ଗାଧୁଏ**.
- Negative: add ନାହିଁ (casual -ନି): ମୁଁ ଡେରିରେ ଶୁଏ ନାହିଁ.
- **ସବୁଦିନ** every day · **ସାଧାରଣତଃ** usually.

sentences.en: I get up at seven every day.
Dad gets up at five every day.
On Saturdays we get up late.
What time do you go to bed?
I usually go to bed at eleven.
Do you bathe every day? (familiar)
The kids brush their teeth in the morning.
I don't go to bed late.

tip.title: Then, after, before
tip.body:
- **ତା'ପରେ** 'then, after that' links steps: ମୁଁ ଗାଧୁଏ, ତା'ପରେ ଜଳଖିଆ ଖାଏ.
- **ପରେ** 'after' and **ଆଗରୁ** 'before' come after their word: ଖାଇବା ପରେ 'after eating', ନଅଟା ଆଗରୁ 'before nine'.
- **ଯିବା** 'go' is irregular: ମୁଁ **ଯାଏ**, ତୁମେ **ଯାଅ**, ଆପଣ **ଯାଆନ୍ତି**.

sentences.en: I have a bath, then I eat breakfast.
What time do you go to the office?
Where do you work? (familiar)
I work in Bhubaneswar.
My brother gets back from work at seven.
After eating I study for a bit.
Be back home before nine. (familiar)
I write a little Odia every day.

lessons.title: What are you doing right now?

tip.title: Right now: -ଉଛି
tip.body:
- For what's happening now: ମୁଁ **କରୁଛି**, ତୁମେ **କରୁଛ**, ଆପଣ **କରୁଛନ୍ତି**, ଆମେ **କରୁଛୁ**, ସେ **କରୁଛି**.
- Vowel stems: ଖାଉଛି, ଯାଉଛି, ଗାଧୋଉଛି.
- Negative: ମୁଁ ଦେଖୁ **ନାହିଁ** (casual ଦେଖୁନି).
- As in English it can mean the near future: ମୁଁ ଆସୁଛି 'I'm coming'.

sentences.en: What are you doing? (formal)
Dad is watching TV.
What are you looking at? (familiar)
Are you listening to me? (familiar)
I'm studying now — I'll come later.
We're having tea — come and join us!
My brother is having a bath right now.
I can't hear anything.
Can I sit here?

tip.title: Give, take, wash
tip.body:
- **ଦେବା** give: ମୁଁ / ସେ **ଦିଏ**, ଆପଣ **ଦିଅନ୍ତି**; right now: **ଦେଉଛି**.
- **ନେବା** take: ମୁଁ **ନିଏ**, ଆପଣ **ନିଅନ୍ତି**; right now: **ନେଉଛି**.
- **ଧୋଇବା** wash: ମୁଁ **ଧୁଏ**; right now: **ଧୋଉଛି**.
- **ବେଳେବେଳେ** sometimes.

sentences.en: Mum is cooking in the kitchen.
Dad sometimes cooks.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଲୁଗା ଧୋଉଛି, ପରେ ଫୋନ କରିବି।
sentences.roman: muṃ luga dhouchhi, pôre phonô kôribi.
sentences.en: I'm washing clothes — I'll call you later.
I wash the plates every day.
Dad wears white clothes every day.
He gives me tea every day.
I don't take sugar.
Who's cooking today?

tip.title: How often, and going to do things
tip.body:
- **ସବୁଦିନ** every day · **ସବୁବେଳେ** always · **ସାଧାରଣତଃ** usually · **ବେଳେବେଳେ** sometimes — they go before the verb.
- 'Go and do something': verb + **-ବାକୁ** + ଯିବା: ଚାଲିବାକୁ ଯାଏ 'I go for a walk', ଖେଳିବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି 'is off to play'.
- **ଏକାଠି** together · **ଚାଲ!** 'come on, let's go!'

sentences.en: The kids play outside in the evening.
We play together on Sundays.
Do you go for a walk every day?
My brother is off to play now.
I walk for an hour every day.
He's always late.
Come on, let's eat together.
Come over to our place sometimes.
